title: Amount in words in RDLC reports (Lakh and Crore, any currency)
summary: Paste one block of VB code into your RDLC report and print any amount in words, in lakhs and crores, for INR and 15 other currencies.

title: Commit every 100 records in AL with mod
summary: A tiny pattern for long-running batch jobs so one failure doesn't roll back hours of work.

title: Why `exit` doesn't skip a record in a report
summary: Calling exit in OnAfterGetRecord leaves the trigger but the row is still printed. Use CurrReport.Skip().

title: Ship a PermissionSet object with every extension
summary: A complete starter permission set so users can be assigned access the moment your extension is installed.

title: N+1 queries in AL: why a simple loop makes Business Central slow, and how to fix it
summary: A loop that looks harmless can send thousands of extra SQL statements. Learn to spot the N+1 pattern in AL, measure it, and fix it four ways.

title: Stop storing API keys in a Business Central field: use Isolated Storage and a masked field
summary: Keep API keys and passwords out of your setup table. Store them encrypted in Isolated Storage, show them masked on the page, and read them back as SecretText.

title: Show request and response JSON in colour on a Business Central page (WebPageViewer)
summary: Build a log page that shows the request and response JSON side by side, indented and colour-coded like a code editor, using the built-in WebPageViewer and a small recursive procedure.

title: SingleInstance vs BindSubscription: run an event subscriber only when you want it
summary: Need a subscriber to run only during your own process, not every time a user works? See why a SingleInstance flag is risky, and how BindSubscription solves it cleanly.

title: Encryption explained like a story: hashing, AES, RSA, keys, IV and chaining (Part 1)
summary: No coding knowledge needed. Locked boxes, fingerprints, padlocks and suitcases explain hashing, AES, RSA, public and private keys, IV and chaining in plain words.

title: Merge PDFs in Business Central with pure AL (no ControlAddIn, no Azure), and one problem I need your help with
summary: Upload any number of PDFs on a page and download them as one merged file, using only AL and the report OnPreRendering trigger. It works, but the result starts with one blank page. What I tried, and a request for your ideas.

title: How CBC and the IV really work: 10 questions everyone asks, answered with one real example
summary: Why is the message cut into pieces? Doesn't mixing 16 + 16 bytes give 32? Where does the IV go, and how does the receiver decrypt? One real AES example, followed step by step.

title: Calling an API from AL: what I wish someone had told me about HttpClient and headers
summary: Request, response, headers, content... When I started with integrations, these words confused me more than the code. Here is how I understand them now, with GET, POST and PATCH examples in AL you can try today.

title: JsonObject, JsonArray, JsonToken, JsonValue: how I finally understood JSON in AL
summary: Four JSON types with confusing names. Once I pictured them as a cupboard, boxes and a parcel, reading JSON in AL became easy. Let's read a real order together, step by step, and write one back.

title: BC 29 changes how table extensions are stored, and why your keys just got more powerful
summary: From Business Central version 29, your table extension fields sit in the same SQL table as the base table. What changed, why it matters for keys, the story of how we got here, and 12 "Did you know?" facts on keys, Blobs and SetLoadFields, each explained simply.

title: Show purchase totals and GST without slowing down the page: Page Background Tasks in AL
summary: Users wanted to see line totals and GST on the Purchase Order itself, but calculating them made the page slow. Page Background Tasks let the page open at once and fill the totals a moment later. Here is how it works, step by step.

title: "Document is out of balance": why journals created by code or APIs fail, and how to find the line that's off
summary: Your code or API creates journal lines, and posting stops with "out of balance by 200". Here is how Business Central checks the balance, the seven usual causes, a small AL tool that points to the exact document, and how to build journal lines that always balance.

title: ReadIsolation in AL, explained with one simple example
summary: Forget the definitions. Let's take one budget line, two users and one moment in time, and replay it once for each ReadIsolation level. By the end you'll know exactly what each level does and when to use it. Part 1 of a short series on locking.

title: What is a lock, and what does LockTable really lock?
summary: Using the same IT budget example as part 1, let's see what a lock is, how long it lives, and why LockTable doesn't lock the whole table the moment you call it. Part 2 of a short series on locking.

title: Commit() in AL: what I wish someone had told me earlier
summary: For a long time I thought Commit() meant "save". It doesn't, and that misunderstanding can quietly break your data. Here's what I learned about Commit, the hidden commit in Codeunit.Run, and how CommitBehavior protects your code from other people's commits. Part 3 of a short series on locking.

title: No. Series in AL, simply explained: GetNextNo, PeekNextNo, and how to number a new document
summary: GetNextNo takes a number. PeekNextNo only looks at it. That one difference decides whether your documents get clean numbers or duplicates. Here's how No. Series works, how to give a number to a new record the way Business Central does, when PeekNextNo is the right choice, and when to use the batch version.

title: How to apply a payment to an invoice from AL code (3 simple ways)
summary: A user can apply a payment to an invoice in two clicks. Doing the same from AL code is not so obvious. Here are three simple ways to do it, with code, and the small mistakes to avoid. I learned this by reading blogs and the Business Central base app code.

title: GST explained simply: from "what is GST" to "why is GST not coming in BC"
summary: GST in simple words, the way I finally understood it. Who actually pays GST, where CGST, SGST and IGST money goes, registered and unregistered vendors, input credit and GSTR-2B, reverse charge, and at the end a Business Central checklist for when GST is not coming.

title: What happens when you post a purchase in Business Central? Every entry, step by step
summary: Purchase posting explained for developers with zero finance background. We start with the simplest purchase (one G/L line, no tax), then add GST, then an item, then mix both, then TDS and reverse charge. One small step at a time, with every entry BC creates and why.

title: Direct Paste: copy rows from Excel and paste them straight into Business Central (open source)
summary: I built a small free tool called Direct Paste. You copy rows from Excel, paste them in Business Central, check the columns once, and BC checks every row before saving anything. Here's how it looks and how I made it work.

title: Unique = true on a secondary key: what it does, and how I found it by accident
summary: My table's primary key was Entry No., but BC still refused to insert the same record twice. The reason was one line I hadn't noticed, Unique = true on a secondary key. Here's what it does, how it differs from the primary key, and why it beats the usual SetRange + FindFirst + Error check.

title: Why does my Entry No. skip numbers? AutoIncrement gaps, explained
summary: Entry No. goes 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, then 7. Nobody deleted number 6. AutoIncrement is designed to leave gaps, and once you know why, you'll know when it's the right choice and when you need something else.

title: Dimensions in Business Central: how one Dimension Set ID holds all your dimensions
summary: Every posted entry in BC carries just one number for all its dimensions, the Dimension Set ID. Same combination, same number, every time, in any order. I'll explain what dimensions are, how BC finds that number using a small "notebook" table, and how to work with dimensions in AL.
